Elles seront utilisées par des personnels qualifiées, 8h par jour pendant 200 jours par an en moyenne.

title: Germany – Test drilling and boring work – ABS 38 Nacherkundungsleistungen Entwässerungsplanung, PA03 Abschnitt Ost
description: Zur Konkretisierung der Entwässerungsplanung im Projekt ABS 38, Abschnitt Ost (PA03) ist die genaue Ermittlung der Versickerungsfähigkeit des Untergrunds erforderlich. Mit den ausgeschriebenen Arbeiten sollen die Versickerungskennwerte in Situ ermittelt werden. Damit werden die Voraussetzungen für eine genauere Planung geschaffen und Risiken in der Bauausführung gemindert. Es handelt sich hierbei um folgende Arbeiten: Baustelle einrichten, Einmessen der Aufschlusspunkte ca. 1.200 Stk. einschließlich Bohranzeige und Geokoordinaten, Vorschachtungen ca.1.200 Stk., Bohrlöcher für Absenkversuche herstellen ca. 1.600 m, Bohrlöcher verfüllen ca. 1.600 m, Erkundungsschürfe herstellen ca. 495 Stk. in unterschiedlichen Tiefen von 1,25 bis zu 5 m, Erkundungsschürfe klein herstellen ca. 470 Stk. in Tiefen von 0,5 bis 1,25 m, Versickerungsversuche ca. 965 Stk. einschl. Protokollierung zur Bestimmung der Versickerungsfähigkeit des Untergrunds nach DWA A 138-1, Open End Test ca. 320 Stk. einschl. Protokollierung zur Bestimmung der Versickerungsfähigkeit des Untergrunds nach DIN 19682-8

title: Access Control and Intrusion Detection Services
description: The Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) requires the provision of parts and labour (technical support, programming, installation, service, and maintenance) on an “as and when requested” basis for its Integrated Security System (ISS) at CRA locations across Canada. The CRA is considering the conversion of up to 51 sites currently using a combination of Digital Security Controls (DSC) Intrusion Detection Systems and Kantech Access Control systems to a unified Kantech Intrusion/Access Control platform. The site counts identified below represent the CRA’s current intended conversion plans for planning and estimation purposes only and do not constitute a commitment to convert any specific number of sites. The CRA requires the goods and services referenced above in the following regions: 1. National Capital Region (NCR) – up to 11 sites identified for potential conversion; 2. Ontario – up to 13 sites identified for potential conversion; 3. Quebec – up to 1 site identified for potential conversion; 4. Atlantic – up to 4 sites identified for potential conversion; and 5. Western – up to 22 sites identified for potential conversion. Bidders may submit a bid for one (1) or more Regions identified in this RFP. Only one (1) bid submission is required, regardless of the number of Regions for which the Bidder is submitting a bid. The Bidder's submission must clearly identify each Region for which it is proposing to provide the required goods and services. For each Region bid, the Bidder must provide all information required by this RFP, including any Region-specific technical information, resource information, and pricing, in the format prescribed in the bid solicitation documents. Requirement, project experience, certification, corporate qualification, or other bid components that are not Region-specific need only be submitted once and will be evaluated for all Regions included in the Bidder's submission. Bids for Multiple Regions: Requirements identified as Region-specific will be evaluated only for the applicable Region. Requirements that are not Region-specific will be evaluated once and will apply to all Regions included in the Bidder's submission. The CRA will evaluate each Region independently. Where a Bidder fails to meet a Region-specific requirement, the CRA may declare the bid non-responsive for that Region only. For greater certainty, a determination that a bid is non-responsive for one (1) Region will not, in itself, render the Bidder's submission non-responsive for any other Region for which a bid as been submitted, provided all applicable requirements for those Regions are met. The CRA intends to award up to five (5) contracts to fulfill this requirement. A Bidder may be awarded a contract for one (1) Region, multiple Regions, or all five (5) Regions. The period of the resulting contract(s) will be for three (3) firm years. The contract(s) will include four (4) irrevocable one-year options to extend the period of the contract(s). The contract(s) will also include provisions allowing the CRA to add, remove or modify products and sites. A bid must comply with the requirements of the bid solicitation and meet all mandatory evaluation criteria to be declared responsive. For each Region, the responsive bid with the highest combined rating of technical merit and price will be recommended for award of a contract. Each Region will be evaluated separately. Where the same Bidder is ranked first for multiple Regions, the CRA will award a single contract covering the Regions for which that Bidder is the highest-ranked responsive bidder. The Bid Compliance and Remedy Process (BCRP) defined in Part 4.2 will apply. Proposal documents and supporting information must be submitted in either English or French. Questions must be directed in writing to the contracting authority via email: Timothy.Berg@cra-arc.gc.ca Bids must be submitted by using the Connect service provided by the Canada Post Corporation. When responding, the proposal MUST be delivered to: Canada Revenue Agency Bid Receiving Unit BRUg@cra-arc.gc.ca Bids will not be accepted if emailed directly to this email address. This email address must be used to request that CRA open a Connect conversation, as detailed in Standard Instructions 2003. Bidders must not use their own licensing agreement for Connect to initiate a Connect conversation with CRA. The CRA reserves the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. There are security requirements associated with this requirement. For additional information, consult the bid solicitation document. The Federal Contractors Program (FCP) for employment equity applies to this procurement. This bid solicitation 1000536720/B cancels and supersedes previous bid solicitation number 1000536720/A dated 2026-03-27 with a closing of 2026-05-19 02:00 PM EDT. This solicitation is open only to Canadian suppliers and to Suppliers of an applicable trading partner. For additional information, consult the bid solicitation document. The CRA will include the following minimum work guarantees (all applicable taxes included) over the entire period of the resulting contract(s), which includes any exercised option periods, including any extension period thereof: 1. National Capital Region (NCR) – $100,000 CAD; 2. Ontario – $100,000 CAD; 3. Quebec – $50,000 CAD; 4. Atlantic – $50,000 CAD; and 5. Western – $100,000 CAD.

Netherlands – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – DUO-EURAAN-JA-IUCN25100274 Constructiesoftware Wft
description: De Staat der Nederlanden nodigt u als potentiële inschrijver uit om in te schrijven voor de openbare Europese aanbesteding voor de aanschaf van een SAAS-oplossing inzake constructiesoftware voor het kunnen maken en beheren van examenvragen voor de Wet Financieel Toezicht (hierna: Wft). Doel is het afsluiten van een dienstverleningsovereenkomst met één leverancier. Het doel van de Opdracht is het verwerven van constructiesoftware welke gebruikt kan worden om Wft-examens te maken die naar Facet geëxporteerd kunnen worden. Deze examens maken deel uit van het vakbekwaamheidsstelsel Wft. Deze aanbesteding is van toepassing voor het constructiedeel, dus voor enkel de software om de examenvragen te maken en te beheren. Wij zoeken een SAAS-oplossing met het doel: Het faciliteren van DUO om het niveau van zijn huidige dienstverlening, op het gebied van de constructie van examens en de ontvangst door Facet van items (met metadata) voor deze examens te behouden en/of verhogen. De geraamde omvang van de opdracht is door DUO vastgelegd in het inkoopstartformulier en is aangevuld met informatie vanuit de marktconsultatie. De totale geschatte opdrachtwaarde voor 10 jaar (incl. eventuele verlengingen) bedraagt € 2.350.000 excl. btw. Let op: de gegevens die de omvang van de opdracht aangeven zijn een indicatie op basis vanuit het verleden en voor de komende jaren. Aan deze omvang kunnen geen rechten aan worden ontleend.

title: Ireland – Development of residential real estate – CFT 3789–Expression of interest for a Development Partner for the Planning, Detailed Design, Construction, Delivery and Sale of a mixed tenure development at Kishogue Urban Centre, Clonburris, Dublin
description: The Council seeks to identify an Economic Operator to act as a Development Partner to work in collaboration with the Council, to identify the optimal solution for Council owned lands within the adopted Clonburris SDZ located at Kishoge Urban Centre (SDCC Site 06), subsectors KUC-S1, KUC-S2 and KUC-S3 in compliance with the adopted SDZ and the Council’s requirements. The Council’s vision is to deliver a sustainable, high quality neighbourhood for Kishogue Urban Centre as Phase 6 of the Clonburris Development. These social, affordable and cost rental homes will be delivered in accordance with the following supporting national and local policies; Clonburris Strategic Development Zone Planning Scheme, South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2022-2028, Housing For All; A new Housing Plan for Ireland 2030, Housing delivery Action Plan 2022-2026 The development site has an estimated capacity for approximately 640 units (subject to planning permission). The required tenure mix is anticipated to be 120 social housing units to be sold to the Council, a minimum of 260 affordable purchase dwellings to be sold to eligible persons under the Scheme of Priority for Affordable Dwellings and a maximum of 260 cost rental units. The tenure types are to be split by block. Delivery of 900m2 of commercial property split over 3 selected ground floor locations across KUC-S1, KUC-S2 and KUC-S3 to facilitate employment or retail use within the wider development. Progress site identification for 6300 m2 of employment use for future development. A location for the employment use has been identified on the included schematic, this does not have to be the final location. The Council is seeking to identify an economic operator that has the requisite skillset and is considered most capable of working in collaboration with the Council, to identify the optimal solution for the development site in accordance with the SDZ and the Council’s requirement and to deliver it as efficiently as possible.

title: UNI - Bastions Central _ CFC233.00 - Lustrerie sur mesure
description:
L’Université Bastion à Genève fait l’objet d’un projet global de rénovation visant une transformation à la fois architecturale et fonctionnelle de l’ensemble existant. L’objectif des travaux est une revalorisation durable de la structure bâtie, en tenant compte des exigences actuelles en matière d’architecture, d’usage, de technique et d’efficacité énergétique.


L’accent est mis sur le développement respectueux du patrimoine bâti historique, tout en intégrant des standards contemporains sur le plan des infrastructures et de l’expression architecturale. Dans ce contexte, des aspects tels que la qualité des espaces, la flexibilité des usages ainsi qu’une approche architecturale claire jouent un rôle central.


Les travaux ont d’ores et déjà débuté et l’exploitation du site se poursuit actuellement dans un contexte de chantier en cours. La mise en service est prévue pour l’année académique 2027 / 2028.


Cet appel d'offre se déroulera en deux phases. Au premier tour, les soumissionnaires devront fournir les documents demandés ainsi que les échantillons de la lentille et du support en métal, selon les indications de l'appel d'offres. Après analyse des dossiers transmis, 3 candidats seront sélectionnés et invités à participer à la 2e phase en fonction des critères de sélection.

description: Atlantic Technological University (ATU) seeks tenders for the appointment of a suitable contractor for the development and construction of a Veterinary Medical Facility at Atlantic Technological University (ATU), Knocknamona, Letterkenny, Co Donegal. The proposed development comprises a new Veterinary Teaching Hospital for Atlantic Technological University at its Knocknamona Campus in Letterkenny. The facility is intended to provide modern clinical, teaching and research facilities, incorporating small-animal, large-animal and equine functions together with pathology, animal accommodation, external yards and associated infrastructure. The development shall be delivered in a phased approach, with the initial veterinary hospital capable of operating as a self-sufficient clinical facility by December 2028. All relevant documents are appended to this notice. Note: This is the first stage of this competitive procedure whereby any interested party may submit a response to this Suitability Assessment Questionnaire in order to be considered for inclusion on the next stage. Full details of the requirement are included in the documents appended to this notice.

title: Synthetic Signature Generation (SSG) Support Services
description: The Department of the Navy, Naval Surface Warfare Center, Carderock Division (NSWCCD) is soliciting for scientific, engineering, and technical services required for the design, development, fabrication, integration, test, fleet implementation, and maintenance of Synthetic Signature Generation (SSG) based simulation systems. The Government requires support system installations and updates required for the following five categories of Navy fleet training systems: Submarine Team, Navigation, Surface, Surveillance, and On-Board. The Government requires design, development, integration, testing, delivery, installation, and maintenance of fielded systems. The Government requires technical engineering support for simulation and training system capabilities to existing fleet onsite maintenance personnel for the operational systems. The Government also requires support for tactical testing and analysis system configurations for common simulation and tactical subsystems utilized in these trainers. The Government is soliciting this requirement as full-and-open competition. The contract will be awarded as a single award indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity(IDIQ), with Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF) Level of Effort (LOE) CLINs and Cost Only Other Direct Costs (ODCs) CLINs for incidental materials and travel. The contract will be for a period of three years to include three one-year ordering periods.

description: 17 Sept 26 The conformed contract, incorporating Amendments 01 through 04, is now available. 03 Sep 26 Amendment 04 was issued with minor corrections to Attachment 1 Statement of Work and Attachments 3a/3b to correct some links in the pricing matrixes. The proposal due date remains 02 Nov 26. 31 Aug 26 Amendment 03 issued with a revised Attachment 2 SRD, Attachment 3a Pricing Matrix, and removal of Clause H005. Solicitation Due date changed to 02 Nov 26 at 12:00pm CST. 24 Aug 26 Editable PDF versions of the previously released Solicitation and Amendments are available. All other terms and conditions remain unchanged and in full force and effect. Reminder, the Solicitation and Amendments must be signed and included with the proposal submission. 12 August Amendment 02 to revise documents as a result of Q&A. 28 Jul 26 Amendment 01 to revised documents as a result of Q&A. 10 Jul 26 Center Console Refresh addresses critical obsolescence issues within the KC-135 Refueling Tanker aircraft. The US Air Force needs an updated Fuel System (FS), Flight Display System (FDS), and Flight Computer due to obsolescence and is looking for innovative ideas to not only replace but improve these systems with turn-key solutions enabling supportability and future growth. The FS, FDS, Flight Computer, and the future growth/adaptability define the scope of the CCR program. The program scope also includes the addition of autothrottle systems. The anticipated contract will be a Cost-Plus Incentive Fee (CPIF) for EMD, Firm Fixed Price (FFP) for Production and Deployment (P&D), single award indefinite delivery/quantity type contract comprised of One (1) 48-month Base Period with Six (6) 1-Year Option Periods and a projected period of performance from July 2028 to June 2038. title: Fort Rucker, AL Full Food Service
description: The Mission Installation Contracting Command - Installation Readiness Center (MICC IRC) has a requirement from the Army Sustainment Command (ASC) in support of the Logistics Readiness Center (LRC) to procure Full Food Service (FFS) under the Army Food Program to provide quality services in support of the installation food service program that supports the Warfighter with flexible, efficient and cost-effective service. The service outlined encompasses dining facility management functions, to include food receiving and storage, food preparation, food serving, remote site feeding, and facility sanitation at Fort Rucker, AL.

description: 03 Sep 26 Amendment 04 was issued with minor corrections to Attachment 1 Statement of Work and Attachments 3a/3b to correct some links in the pricing matrixes. Reminder, the Solicitation and Amendments must be signed and included with the proposal submission. 12 August Amendment 02 to revise documents as a result of Q&A. 28 Jul 26 Amendment 01 to revised documents as a result of Q&A. 10 Jul 26 Center Console Refresh addresses critical obsolescence issues within the KC-135 Refueling Tanker aircraft. The US Air Force needs an updated Fuel System (FS), Flight Display System (FDS), and Flight Computer due to obsolescence and is looking for innovative ideas to not only replace but improve these systems with turn-key solutions enabling supportability and future growth. The FS, FDS, Flight Computer, and the future growth/adaptability define the scope of the CCR program. The program scope also includes the addition of autothrottle systems. The anticipated contract will be a Cost-Plus Incentive Fee (CPIF) for EMD, Firm Fixed Price (FFP) for Production and Deployment (P&D), single award indefinite delivery/quantity type contract comprised of One (1) 48-month Base Period with Six (6) 1-Year Option Periods and a projected period of performance from July 2028 to June 2038. title: Maintenance Dredging of the Isle au Haut Thoroughfare near Isle au Haut, Maine
description: The Isle au Haut Thoroughfare Federal Navigation Project, located between Isle au Haut, Maine and Kimball Island, Maine on the outskirts of Penobscot Bay, about six miles southeast of Stonington and 25 miles east of Rockland. The Federal Navigation Project consists of a -6-foot Mean Lower Low Water (MLLW) deep by 75-foot wide extending 1,200-foot in length through the shoal in the thoroughfare.The proposed work consists of mechanically dredging approximately 3,355 cubic yards (cy) (1,183 cy required, plus 2,172 cy overdepth) of shoaled material consisting of highly compacted coarse sand and gravel, with areas of cobbles and isolated small boulders from the channel. Due to the material type, a mechanical dredge with the ability to dig highly compacted coarse sand and gravel will be required. The proposed action is to dredge to the authorized depth of -6-foot MLLW plus an additional 1-foot of required advance maintenance with an additional allowable 1-foot of overdepth (e.g. -7-foot MLLW required + 1-foot allowable OD). One-time, advanced maintenance is approved for the entirety of the 1200-foot long authorized channel. The dredged material will be placed at the Flake Island Disposal Site (FIDS) which is approximately 1 nautical mile northwest of the FNP. Placement of the dredged material (sand, gravel and cobble) at Flake Island Disposal Site will benefit both juvenile lobster habitat and juvenile cod by increasing the areas habitat complexity.The anticipated allowable dredging window is between September 15 and April 1 to avoid impacts to spawning shellfish, benthic resources, Essential Fish Habitat (EFH) of federally managed species, threatened and endangered species and interactions with mobile fishing gear.

title: Notice of Opportunity (NOO) U.S. Army Reserve, 88th Readiness Division Energy Savings Performance Contract (ESPC)
description: U.S. Army Reserve, 88th RD has an objective to reduce energy consumption, reduce energy cost, and increase energy resiliency of multiple facilities located in Minnesota and Wisconsin. The 88th RD is seeking to identify additional Energy Conservation Measures (ECMs) that provide measurable energy and cost savings. Potential energy and water saving projects may include but are not limited to: envelope improvements, insulation upgrades, window upgrades, LED upgrades, geothermal heat pumps, lighting, controls, renewable energy generation including photovoltaic solar arrays, retro-commissioning, water conservation measures, heating, ventilation, air conditioning (HVAC) upgrades including boilers, furnaces, split systems, and chillers, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and Hydrogen Fuel Cells and microgrids. Additional ECMs of interest include re-tuning; retro-commissioning and re-commissioning; building automation and control systems; window replacement; minor building-envelope improvements; domestic hot-water system replacement; plug-load analysis and reduction, including refrigerators and freezers; water-leak detection; and other water-efficiency upgrades. The project will evaluate these and other cost-effective opportunities to modernize facilities, improve energy and water resilience, and support the 88th RD long-term energy, water conservation, and resiliency goals (as determined by 88th RD and ARIMD). description: Pre-Solicitation Notice Amendment for Navajo Area Abandoned Mines Response and Construction Services II (AMRCS II). This is a Request for Information (RFI) regarding the attached Draft Request for Proposal (DRFP). The DRFP is being released for COMMENT ONLY. This is not a synopsis proceeding the issuance of a solicitation. It is market research issued solely for information purposes - it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or any other solicitation. This notice does not commit the U.S. Government to contract for any supply or service. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (US EPA) is not seeking proposals at this time. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay any cost incurred in response to this notice. All costs associated with responding to this notice will solely be at the interested parties' expense. Any information provided by industry to the Government as a result of this notice is voluntary. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future solicitation. It is recommended that interested parties monitor the FEDCONNECT website (https://www.fedconnect.net) for any information that may pertain to this notice. The information provided in this notice is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. The purpose of this RFI is to Request Comment on the DRFP for this requirement; which includes potential evaluation criteria for Navajo area- Abandoned Mines Response and Construction Services (AMRCS). To ensure the formal solicitation is executed in the most effective manner possible, we are posting the DRFP to offer an opportunity for industry to provide feedback. Your questions and input will be used to further refine, improve, or clarify these requirements. All Information and documentation posted under this notice are preliminary in nature and may be updated or amended prior to the release of the formal solicitation. NOTICE INFORMATION 1. SOLICITATION NUMBER: 68HE0926R0006 2. TITLE: Navajo Area- Abandoned Mines Response and Construction Services (AMRCS) 3. PRODUCT SERVICE CODE: F108- Hazardous Substance Removal, Cleanup, and Disposal Services 4. NAICS CODE: 562910- Environmental Remediation Services- Environmental Remediation Services a. Size Standard: 750 Employees 5. ANTICIPATED RFP RELEASE: Fall 2026 6. ANTICIPATED CONTRACT TYPE: Single award Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) 7. DESCRIPTION a. Background: Under the authority of Section 104 of the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) or Super fund of 1980, as amended by the Superfund Amendments and Reauthorization Act (SARA); Subtitle I of the Resource Conservation and Recover y Act (RCRA) and pursuant to the National Oil and Hazardous Substances Pollution Contingency Plan (NCP) (40 CFR Part 300); and in accordance with any reauthorizations or amendment s to any of the above named statutes and new response legislation, the EPA has been delegated the responsibility to undertake response actions with respect to the release or threat of release of hazardous substances, or pollutants and contaminants, that pose an actual or potential threat to human health or welfare, or to the environment. b. Navajo Area Uranium Mines (USEPA Region 9) The Navajo Nation encompasses more than 27,000 square miles, spread amongst the Four Corners Region of the USA (Colorado, New Mexico, Utah, and Arizona). The unique geology of the region makes the Navajo Nation rich in uranium, a radioactive ore in high demand after the development of atomic power and weapons at the close of World War II in the 1940s. Approximately four million tons of uranium ore were extracted during mining operations within the Navajo Nation from 1944 to 1986. Many Navajo people worked the mines, often living and raising families in close proximity to the mines and mills. Uranium mining and milling activities no longer occur on Navajo lands, but the legacy of these activities remains, including more than 500 abandoned uranium mine claims with thousands of mine features such as pits, trenches, holes, etc., and homes and drinking water sources with elevated levels of uranium, radium and other radionuclides. Uranium and other elements (selenium, arsenic, etc.) associated with mine and mill sites also occur naturally at elevated levels in rock, soil, surface water, and groundwater across the Navajo Nation and the broader Four Corners region. USEPA maintains a strong partnership with the Navajo Nation and, since 1994, the USEPA Superfund Program has provided technical assistance and funding to assess potentially contaminated sites and develop a response. In August 2007, the USEPA Superfund Program compiled a Comprehensive Database and Atlas of all known uranium mines on the Navajo Nation. In October 2007, at the request of the U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, EPA, along with the Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA), the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC), the Department of Energy (DOE), and the Indian Health Service (IHS) developed a coordinated https://www.epa.gov/navajo-nation-uranium-cleanup to address uranium contamination in consultation with Navajo Nation EPA. d. Region 9 The primary hazardous substance on all the sites referenced in the requirement�s Statement of Work (SOW) is radiological mine and mine related waste; therefore, a significant knowledge base of radiological material handling, environmental data interpretation, and data collection will be required to perform the activities within this SOW. The terrain to access site locations is rough, water is scarce, and the weather is often extreme in most areas. The trails and/or roads to the sites are not improved or maintained. To reach the site locations, 4-wheel drive vehicles (capable of drives over rough dirt/rocky roads) and/or hiking long distances is required. Roads can become impassable in wet weather, and conditions can change quickly. In summer, the conditions are hot and dry; in winter, elevations make them subject to severe cold and high winds. Due to the quick changes in the weather, be aware of the danger of flash floods. While this danger is greatest during the summer monsoon season (July through September), flash floods can occur at any time of the year. e. Purpose and Objectives: The purpose of the Navajo Area Abandoned Mines Response and Construction Services (AMRCS) contract is to provide cleanup, response, and construction services to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), primarily at former uranium mining-related sites on or within the Navajo Nation (within EPA Region 9 in Arizona and New Mexico). 7. DESCRIPTION OF INFORMATION REQUESTED: The USEPA is seeking comments on the attached DRFP. The Government will consider all comments, questions, and issues raised by all prospective offerors in formulating requirements for any resultant solicitation document. The information contained here reflects the Government's anticipated requirements as of the date on this posting. The purpose of this notice is to solicit comments regarding a possible acquisition. The issuance of this notice is designed to gather as much information as possible to ensure that the Government's requirements are clear and concise; and possibly improve the requirements based on industry best practices and lessons learned, which may be stated in a future solicitation. SUBMITTAL INFORMATION A cover page and an executive summary may be included in the response, but is not required. All interested parties may respond. At a minimum, responses should include the following: a. Business name, SAM Unique Entity ID, business address, size and type of business (e.g., Large Business, Small Business, 8(a), HubZone, Woman Owned Small Business etc.) pursuant to the applicable NAICS code, and the name, telephone number, mailing address, and email address of a point of contact having authority and knowledge to discuss responses with Government representatives.

title: Bulgaria – Firearms – "Доставка на 40 mm автоматичен гранатомет – рамково споразумение"
description: Предметът на обществената поръчка включва доставка на до 35 /тридесет и пет/ броя 40 mm автоматичен гранатомет чрез сключване на рамково споразумение. Продуктът представлява автоматично оръжие, предназначено за унищожаване на жива сила в леки укрития от полеви тип и окопи, поразяване на леко бронирани машини, като позволява водене на индиректен огън от закрити огневи позиции. Състава и описанието на продукта, както и тактико-техническите изисквания към продукта, предмет на обществената поръчка са детайлно описани в Техническа спецификация ТС Б 53.4925.25 - ВО, приложение към настоящата документация. Рамковото споразумение ще бъде сключено с едно лице – участникът, класиран на първо място и определен за изпълнител при условията на чл. 82, ал. 1 от ЗОП. Възложителят ще сключва конкретни договори, като прилага тези условия.

buyer: Oslo kommune v/ Oslo Havn KF
title: 35HAV26 - Kjøp av kabelhåndteringssystem (CMS) til Kneppeskjær
description: Oslo Havn KF (HAV) har fått tilsagn støtte fra Enova til et landstrømanlegg på Kneppeskjær. Anlegget må oppfylle kravene i tildelingsbrevet fra Enova. Dette omfatter blant annet kravene i NEK IEC PAS 80005-3. Leverandør av landstrømanlegget og uttaksskap er allerede tildelt, og arbeidet på kaien er påbegynt. Landstrømanlegget skal forsyne skip på Kneppeskjær kai på Sjursøya. Kneppeskjær kai er delt i to deler: øst og vest. Det skal være tre uttaksskap og være dimensjonert for en effekt på 1600 kVA ved 690 V og 50 Hz. Denne anskaffelsen omfatter kjøp av tre kabelhåndteringssystemer (CMS, Cable Management System) som skal brukes til å koble kablene mellom uttaksskap/grensesnittskap og skipene. Dette inkluderer 1 stk. kabeltårn for CCS-skip og 2. stk mobile kabelhåndteringssystem. Betegnelsen CMS vil brukes som en fellesbetegnelse for de tre kabelhåndteringssystemene. Anskaffelsen omfatter også en treårig serviceavtale for kabeltårnet og en treårig serviceavtale for de mobile kabelhåndteringssystemene. I tillegg inkluderer anskaffelsen følgende opsjoner: Opsjon 1: 2 stk. mobile kabelhåndteringssystemer Opsjon 2: Tilkoblinger etter prøvedrift Opsjon 3: Reserveplugger Opsjon 4: Blindkontakter Opsjon 5: Garanti Opsjon 6: Serviceavtale Leverandøren er anvarlig for koordinering med leverandøren av landstrømanlegget (Powercon). Oppdragsgiver ønsker de mobile kabelhåndteringssysteme og kabeltårnet skal leveres så snart som mulig, senest innen 12 måneder etter kontraktinngåelse. Leverandøren skal som del av sitt tilbud angi leveringstid for kabeltårn og de mobile kabelhåndteringsystemene.

buyer: Oslo kommune v/ Oslo Havn KF
title: Norway – Electricity distribution and control apparatus – 35HAV26 - Procurement of a cable management system (CMS) for Kneppeskjær
description: The Port of Oslo (HAV) has received support from Enova for an on-shore power plant at Kneppeskjær. The facility must meet the requirements in the award letter from Enova. This includes i.a. the requirements in NEK IEC PAS 80005-3. The supplier of the land power system and power cabinets has already been awarded, and work on the quay has begun. The land power plant shall supply the ship at Kneppeskjær quay on Sjursøya. The kneppeskjær quay is divided into two parts: east and west. There shall be three extraction cabinets and dimensioned for an output of 1600 kVA at 690 V and 50 Hz. This procurement is for the procurement of three cable management systems (CMS, Cable Management System) that shall be used to connect the cables between the socket cupboards/interface cabinets and the ships. This includes 1 cable tower for CCS ships and 2 mobile cable handling systems. The term CMS will be used as a generic term for the three cable handling systems. The procurement also includes a three year service agreement for the cable tower and a three year service contract for the mobile cable handling systems. In addition the procurement includes the following options: Option 1: 2 mobile cable management systems. Option 2: Connections after trial operation Option 3: Spare plugs Option 4: Blind contacts Option 5: Guarantee Option 6: Service contract The tenderer is required to be coordinated with the supplier of the land power system (Powercon). The contracting authority would like the mobile cable management systems and the cable tower shall be delivered as soon as possible, at the latest within 12 months after the contract has been signed. Tenderers shall, as part of their tender, state the delivery time for cable towers and the mobile cable management systems.

description: September 28, 2026 Please see attached Compiled EOI and Appendices_V2 DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY Expression of Interest�DOE�s Office of Environmental Management (DOE-EM) Critical Minerals and Materials Inventory. SUMMARY: The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) Office of Environmental Management (EM) publishes the following questions regarding potential collaboration with interested parties for the reuse of its critical and rare earth minerals and materials. The goal is to ensure surplus critical minerals and materials within the DOE inventory are repurposed to bolster and diversify the U.S. supply chain. This will support domestic scientific, manufacturing, and energy needs. A list of materials and minerals in DOE�s inventory is supplied as an attachment. Respondents should note that industry partners would be responsible for the subsequent extraction or reprocessing of the material. THIS IS AN EXPRESSION OF INTEREST ONLY. THIS NOTICE DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A NOTICE OF FUNDING OPPORTUNITY (NOFO). A NOFO DOES NOT EXIST AT THIS TIME. title: Request for Information - Energetics Center of Excellence
description: Request for Information - Energetics Center of Excellence 1.0 Purpose Army Contracting Command�Rock Island, on behalf of Portfolio Acquisition Executive Agile Sustainment & Ammunition and Project Lead Joint Services, is requesting information from industry regarding transformative projects, programs, capabilities, and concepts that would strengthen the Department of War (DoW) energetics ecosystem and resiliency within the Defense Industrial Base (DIB). This Request for Information (RFI) is intended to inform potential use of funding for energetics resilience at Blue Grass Army Depot (BGAD) in Richmond, Kentucky. The Government is intentionally non-prescriptive regarding detailed technical or product requirement through this RFI. Rather, the Government seeks industry input on both defense and commercially executable solutions that address energetic-resiliency challenges through a potential Private-Public Partnership (P3). This request for information is for market research purposes only and is not a formal contract offer. Your response cannot be accepted to form a binding contract, and the Army is not at this time seeking proposals. 2.0 Problem Statement The DoW energetics enterprise faces increasing demand while portions of the supporting industrial base remain constrained by limited domestic capacity, aging infrastructure, legacy manufacturing processes, long qualification timelines, and fragile or concentrated supply chains. These constraints pose a risk to warfighter readiness, ability to rapidly scale during periods of additional demand, and constrain the ability to field next generation munitions. 3.0 Scope and Desired Solutions Industry may propose concepts across the full energetics spectrum or energetics value chain that include discrete projects, multiple coordinated but independently executable project modules, or a master-campus concept involving complementary capabilities. The Government seeks practical, scalable, and commercially sustainable solutions during future periods of low to no government orders that may include, but are not limited to: Onshoring: Establishing domestic production capacity for energetics products, inputs, components, precursors, or processing capabilities currently produced OCONUS. Supply-Chain Resilience: Reducing foreign, sole-source, or other critical supply-chain dependencies; increasing domestic redundancy; and eliminating or mitigating single-point production failures. Flexible Production Capacity: Modernizing, supplementing, or replacing legacy manufacturing and processing methods through automation, digital process control, flexible manufacturing (modular, reconfigurable, multi-product production lines that can support multiple products, formulations, customers, or demand scenarios), advanced quality assurance, continuous or semi-continuous processing, or similar approaches to create the flexibility needed to quickly scale up for surge requirements. Next-Generation Formulation Transition: Establish medium-scale production and scale-up capability to accelerate transition of next-generation formulations from small scale lab to production-representative and full-rate manufacturing. Commercially Sustainable Operations: Establishing a dual-use, single/multi-tenant, or other commercial model capable of sustaining operations through peacetime by utilizing widely available commercial industry processes, manufacturing, and materials while retaining readiness to support defense surge requirements. 4.0 Threshold Criteria and Limitations Respondents have broad latitude regarding the solution proposed. However, each concept should meet the following threshold criteria and limitations. 4.1 Geographic Location � BGAD, Richmond, Kentucky All proposed physical facilities, pilot lines, processing units, laboratories, capital improvements, and associated support infrastructure must be located at BGAD. 4.2 DIB Synergy and Alignment Proposed capabilities must be new, unique, and complete or provide complementary, supplementary, or redundant/resilient production capabilities within the existing Contractor-Owned, Contractor-Operated (COCO), Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO), and Government-Owned, Government-Operated (GOGO) Army network. 4.3 Commercial Viability and No Planned Recurring Government Support The Government seeks concepts that do not rely on planned recurring U.S. Government funding for steady-state facility operations, maintenance, staffing, overhead, or routine upkeep after establishment. The Government would be interested in respondent, commercial, or third-party co-investment, where applicable. 4.4 Schedule The Government is seeking a Period of Performance (PoP) of 48 months or less to achieve full project transition and commissioning. The Army is focused on rapid capability acceleration, earlier completion timelines are highly encouraged. 5.0 Submission Requirements Responses are limited to a maximum of 10 pages, which must detail the following: Project description and expected warfighter / DIB impact; Technical approach, modernization method, and next-generation formulation transition plan; Commercial products or services utilization to keep the facility viable during period of low to no USG orders; Onshoring, supply-chain resilience, and foreign-dependency reduction benefits; Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) that includes the cost for design, construction, and commissioning, rationale for dual-use sustainable business model, and optional self/co-investment; Execution milestones to the complete path within 48 months or less. 6.0 Point of Contact and Submission Deadline Industry is requested to submit responses to this RFI no later than 4:00pm central 02 November 2026. Responses and questions regarding this RFI shall be submitted to: Contracting Officer: SFC Pramod Khanal at pramod.khanal.mil@army.mil Contract Specialist: Lindsey Arguello at lindsey.j.arguello.civ@army.mil 7.0 Industry Day The Government plans to have further conversation with industry and shape the Energetics Center of Excellence requirement at the GOCO Industry Day in November 2026 referenced here: https://sam.gov/workspace/contract/opp/73cb195b4756453494768ade061e21aa/view. Industry Day details and registration information will be provided in a subsequent update to the GOCO Industry Day announcement. Registration is not required at this time. Disclaimer The Government does not intend to reimburse any contractor for any information or administrative costs associated with responding to this notification. Participation in this survey is strictly voluntary. Any information stated above is subject to change. Respondents are responsible for appropriately marking any proprietary information. This is a Sources Sought notice for market research purposes only and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a commitment to issue an RFP in the future.

description: Request for Information - Energetics Center of Excellence 1.0 Purpose Army Contracting Command�Rock Island, on behalf of Portfolio Acquisition Executive Agile Sustainment & Ammunition and Project Lead Joint Services, is requesting information from industry regarding transformative projects, programs, capabilities, and concepts that would strengthen the Department of War (DoW) energetics ecosystem and resiliency within the Defense Industrial Base (DIB). This Request for Information (RFI) is intended to inform potential use of funding for energetics resilience at Blue Grass Army Depot (BGAD) in Richmond, Kentucky. The Government is intentionally non-prescriptive regarding detailed technical or product requirement through this RFI. Rather, the Government seeks industry input on both defense and commercially executable solutions that address energetic-resiliency challenges through a potential Private-Public Partnership (P3). This request for information is for market research purposes only and is not a formal contract offer. Your response cannot be accepted to form a binding contract, and the Army is not at this time seeking proposals. 2.0 Problem Statement The DoW energetics enterprise faces increasing demand while portions of the supporting industrial base remain constrained by limited domestic capacity, aging infrastructure, legacy manufacturing processes, long qualification timelines, and fragile or concentrated supply chains. These constraints pose a risk to warfighter readiness, ability to rapidly scale during periods of additional demand, and constrain the ability to field next generation munitions. 3.0 Scope and Desired Solutions Industry may propose concepts across the full energetics spectrum or energetics value chain that include discrete projects, multiple coordinated but independently executable project modules, or a master-campus concept involving complementary capabilities. The Government seeks practical, scalable, and commercially sustainable solutions during future periods of low to no government orders that may include, but are not limited to: Onshoring: Establishing domestic production capacity for energetics products, inputs, components, precursors, or processing capabilities currently produced OCONUS. Supply-Chain Resilience: Reducing foreign, sole-source, or other critical supply-chain dependencies; increasing domestic redundancy; and eliminating or mitigating single-point production failures. Flexible Production Capacity: Modernizing, supplementing, or replacing legacy manufacturing and processing methods through automation, digital process control, flexible manufacturing (modular, reconfigurable, multi-product production lines that can support multiple products, formulations, customers, or demand scenarios), advanced quality assurance, continuous or semi-continuous processing, or similar approaches to create the flexibility needed to quickly scale up for surge requirements. Next-Generation Formulation Transition: Establish medium-scale production and scale-up capability to accelerate transition of next-generation formulations from small scale lab to production-representative and full-rate manufacturing. Commercially Sustainable Operations: Establishing a dual-use, single/multi-tenant, or other commercial model capable of sustaining operations through peacetime by utilizing widely available commercial industry processes, manufacturing, and materials while retaining readiness to support defense surge requirements. 4.0 Threshold Criteria and Limitations Respondents have broad latitude regarding the solution proposed. However, each concept should meet the following threshold criteria and limitations. 4.1 Geographic Location � BGAD, Richmond, Kentucky All proposed physical facilities, pilot lines, processing units, laboratories, capital improvements, and associated support infrastructure must be located at BGAD. 4.2 DIB Synergy and Alignment Proposed capabilities must be new, unique, and complete or provide complementary, supplementary, or redundant/resilient production capabilities within the existing Contractor-Owned, Contractor-Operated (COCO), Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO), and Government-Owned, Government-Operated (GOGO) Army network. 4.3 Commercial Viability and No Planned Recurring Government Support The Government seeks concepts that do not rely on planned recurring U.S. Government funding for steady-state facility operations, maintenance, staffing, overhead, or routine upkeep after establishment. The Government would be interested in respondent, commercial, or third-party co-investment, where applicable. 4.4 Schedule The Government is seeking a Period of Performance (PoP) of 48 months or less to achieve full project transition and commissioning. The Army is focused on rapid capability acceleration, earlier completion timelines are highly encouraged. 5.0 Submission Requirements Responses are limited to a maximum of 10 pages, which must detail the following: Project description and expected warfighter / DIB impact; Technical approach, modernization method, and next-generation formulation transition plan; Commercial products or services utilization to keep the facility viable during period of low to no USG orders; Onshoring, supply-chain resilience, and foreign-dependency reduction benefits; Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) that includes the cost for design, construction, and commissioning, rationale for dual-use sustainable business model, and optional self/co-investment; Execution milestones to the complete path within 48 months or less. 6.0 Point of Contact and Submission Deadline Industry is requested to submit responses to this RFI no later than 4:00pm central 02 November 2026. Responses and questions regarding this RFI shall be submitted to: Contracting Officer: SFC Pramod Khanal at pramod.khanal.mil@army.mil Contract Specialist: Lindsey Arguello at lindsey.j.arguello.civ@army.mil 7.0 Industry Day The Government plans to have further conversation with industry and shape the Energetics Center of Excellence requirement at the GOCO Industry Day in November 2026 referenced here: https://sam.gov/workspace/contract/opp/73cb195b4756453494768ade061e21aa/view. Industry Day details and registration information will be provided in a subsequent update to the GOCO Industry Day announcement. Registration is not required at this time. Disclaimer The Government does not intend to reimburse any contractor for any information or administrative costs associated with responding to this notification. Participation in this survey is strictly voluntary. Any information stated above is subject to change. Respondents are responsible for appropriately marking any proprietary information. This is a Sources Sought notice for market research purposes only and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a commitment to issue an RFP in the future.

title: DPAA Papua New Guinea Helicopter Requirement
description: The United States Transportation Command (USTRANSCOM) is seeking proposals for rotary-wing aviation support services in Papua New Guinea on behalf of the Defense POW/MIA Accounting Agency (DPAA). The requirement demands providing up to three (3) helicopters simultaneously to support up to three (3) remote recovery missions per year (ranging from 14 to 90 days each), including passenger/cargo transport, sling load operations, and 24/7 on-call MEDEVAC. Offerors are advised to thoroughly review the full solicitation package, paying close attention to the instructions and evaluation criteria outlined in the FAR 52.212-1 and FAR 52.212-2 clauses along with the ten (10) attached documents. A virtual Pre-Proposal Conference will be held via MS Teams on Monday, 27 July 2026, at 10:30 AM CST; meeting access details will be posted on SAM.gov prior to the event. title: Environmental Science and Engineering Contract, A-E Services to be Ordered on Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity Schedule
description: THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE HAS BEEN UPDATED, SEEKING SF330 SUBMITALS. THERE IS NO RFP PACKAGE TO DOWNLOAD. ALL INFORMATION NEEDED TO SUBMIT SF330 DOCUMENT IS CONTAINED HEREIN. SF 254S AND SF 255S WILL NOT BE CONSIDERED. NOTE: FAR PART 12 (COMMERCIAL) IS NOT APPLICABLE TO THIS PROCUREMENT. SUMMARY: The Naval Facilities Engineering and Expeditionary Warfare Center (NAVFAC EXWC), Port Hueneme, California is soliciting SF330s for a single-award, Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ), Architect and Engineering (A-E) contract for various environmental restoration (ER) and other environmental projects. The A-E services required will include professional services to enable NAVFAC EXWC to support other NAVFAC commands, as well as other Department of War (DoW) and federal agencies. Market research was conducted in May 2026 and there were too few qualified small businesses to warrant consideration of a set-aside, therefore this acquisition is being issued under Full and Open Competition. The North American industry Classification System (NAICS) code is the procurement 541330, and the annual size standard is $25,500,000. NAVFAC EXWC anticipates the award of an IDIQ with base ordering period of sixty (60) months, and an extension of services period not to exceed six months. The maximum value of all task order placed under this contract will not exceed $150,000,000. Individual task orders under this contract may be firm fixed price (FFP) (Estimated 40%) or cost-plus-fixed fee (CPFF) (Estimated 60%). The minimum guarantee for the IDIQ contract is $10,000. Individual task orders are anticipated to range $5,000 to $6,000,000 per task order. The estimated award date is March 2027. PROJECT INFORMATION: Firms must be capable of performing work on a wide variety of projects in Environmental Restoration (ER) and other environmental topics, in a manner that complies with federal, state, and local regulations and laws, and within timeframes required. This work will support the A-E services that NAVFAC EXWC provides to support the environmental cleanup of sites managed by the Department of the Navy and other federal agencies. Although, the majority of the work is expected to be in the continental United States, project sites could be worldwide. Specific needs will be determined based upon project requirements and as described in each task order�s Performance Work Statement or Statement of Work. A-E services required under this contract include, but are not limited to: - Environmental program development and implementation. Particularly, the contractor will support development and implementation of the Navy�s environmental restoration (ER) program, comprising the Installation Restoration (IR) and Munitions Response (MR) Programs in terms of the associated science and engineering, regulations, and policy - Research, development, testing, and evaluation (RDT&E) of innovative environmental technologies, techniques, and solutions, particularly for environmental restoration. - Planning and pilot-testing innovative environmental technologies, techniques, investigations, and solutions to support full-scale design. - Services for associated environmental programs, including remedy resilience, impacts of elevated sea water levels and extreme weather events, active range sustainability, sustainable water resources management, environmental compliance, energy efficiency, and natural resources management. The services at ER sites may involve supporting NAVFAC EXWC in the preparation, expert review, or optimization of preliminary assessments, site inspections, remedial investigations, feasibility studies, engineering evaluation/analysis (EECA), proposed plans, records of decision (RODs), remedial designs, sampling and analysis plans (SAPs) or Quality Assurance Project Plans (QAPPs), and five-year reviews for customers in the Department of the Navy and other federal agencies. These services may include site characterization, laboratory studies, and pilot testing with the aim of helping NAVFAC EXWC and its customers develop cost-effective full-scale designs and solutions for environmental projects. An important component of the services also is technology transfer (T2) to and training of the Department of the Navy and other federal agency personnel (and their contractors), who are engaged in ER or other environmental programs. Other environmental project areas may include (but are not limited to) remedy resilience, coastal flooding from seawater and groundwater, and extreme weather events, active range sustainability, sustainable water resource management, environmental compliance, energy efficiency, and natural resource management. For on-site investigations, firms must provide personnel with current health and safety training, as required by the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) and adhere to all NAVFAC requirements for Health and Safety. Task orders will be issued with a project/site specific Scope of Work under the general scope of the contract. Typically, requests for proposals issued for individual task orders will include a general Scope of Work or a performance-based acquisition Performance Work Statement, location of work, character and extent of services required, technical requirements in addition to the requirements contained within Statement of Architect and Engineering Services (SAES). SELECTION CRITERIA: The selection criteria are listed below in descending order of importance. Items (1) thru (5) are primary criteria and (6) thru (7) are secondary criteria. Secondary criteria will only be used as 'tie-breakers' among technically equal firms. (1) Professional Qualifications: Professional Qualifications: The offeror shall provide no more than thirteen (13) resumes in Section E of the Standard Form (SF) 330. If more resumes are submitted than requested, then only the first thirteen will be considered. Providing less resumes is encouraged if provided personnel fulfill multiple roles. Experience that is not related to the work described in this solicitation should not be included. Resumes shall not be more than 2 pages each. Firms will be evaluated in terms of the general professional qualifications and technical competence in areas of work described in the "Project Information" section above. The evaluation of the resumes will consider education, training, registration, certifications, overall and relevant experience, and longevity with the firm. Projects that demonstrate successful optimization efforts that reduced project cost or time and added unique technical value, successful execution of projects where standards and methods for execution were not commonly accepted, or projects that had complex hydrogeological and regulatory site conditions will be given preference. Additionally, projects performed for the Navy or DoW as opposed to other federal agencies or other clients are preferred. Experience on the resumes should be within the last 8 years to be considered relevant. Resumes should be presented in the following three categories: Program Manager (PGM), Project Managers (PMs), and Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) in the technical areas listed above. The PGM and PMs should have a degree in engineering (environmental, civil, chemical, or related), or geological sciences, professional registrations in at least one state of the United States, and at least five (5) years of experience in managing programs or projects of similar size and complexity as expected in this contract. The states of registration and certification of relevant personnel must be included on each resume in Section E of SF 330. description:
Le présent appel d’offres, lancé en procédure ouverte soumise à l’AIMP, porte sur un mandat pour un groupement pluridisciplinaire (ingénieur civil pilote, architecte paysagiste, ingénieur en mobilité, ingénieur en environnement, arboriste, spécialiste lumière / éclairage, géomètre et géotechnicien) pour le réaménagement des trois voiries communales du quartier de Surville.

title: One Photonic Wafer Probe Station and one Photonic Assembly Station
description: This tender concerns DTU Nano's planned procurement of a Photonic Assembly Station and a Photonic Wafer Probe Station. The tender is split into to two lots – one for each of the two stations. Tenderers may choose to bid on one or both lots, which will be evaluated and awarded individually. The assembly station is for connecting fibre array units (FAUs) to an optical chip. The type of connection will be edge coupling using waveguides loops for alignment but if necessary, the alignment can also be performed either using the light source on the chip (if it exists) or by using an external light source and connecting two FAUs, one on each side of the chip. Thus, the main purpose of the machine is to do assembly and fiber attachment of photonic chips. The system shall support research, prototyping, process development, pilot manufacturing, and low-volume production activities within DTU Nano's advanced fabrication facility. DTU has activities within Silicon Photonics (SiPh), Photonic Integrated Circuits (PICs), Optical transceivers, Laser modules, Photodetectors, Fiber-optic assemblies, Co-packaged optics and Quantum photonic devices which we want to support in the best possible way. DTU therefore intends to purchase a reconfigurable, flexible, versatile machine. The purpose of the photonic wafer probe station is to characterise the quality of photonic integrated circuits (PICs). It should be possible to characterise both optical and electrical performance. For the optical characterisation, the main coupling in/out technique will be through grating couplers, but the equipment should be possible to be configured also for edge coupling to component facets in a grove on the wafer. In this case, different holders and fibres may be needed. The electrical characteristics are to be characterised both in DC as well as RF up to 40GHz using probe and/or probe cards. The system shall support research, development, process qualification, and routine characterization activities within DTU Nano's advanced fabrication facility.

title: Ombygning af Aabenraa genbrugsplads
description: Arwos driver i dag en genbrugsplads med genbrugsbutik i Aabenraa. Arwos ønsker at skabe en fremtidssikret genbrugsplads, hvor det er muligt at udfolde initiativerne i den kommunale affaldsplan for Aabenraa Kommune. Affaldsplanens initiativer er fokuseret på cirkulær økonomi med mere direkte genbrug, salg i egen butik og samarbejder omkring ressourcer og partnerskaber. Nærværende projekt er betegnet som ”Ombygning af Aabenraa genbrugsplads” (herefter benævnt ”Projektet”). Projektet består i at gentænke genbrugspladsens funktion, indretning og drift med henblik på at etablere en fremtidssikret genbrugsplads. Projektet realiseres som en totalentreprise, hvor den valgte totalentreprenør får ansvaret for såvel projektering som udførelse af den endelige løsning. Bygherre har ikke på forhånd fastlagt den endelige løsning eller den nærmere tilrettelæggelse af totalentreprisen. Udbuddet gennemføres som en konkurrencepræget dialog, jf. udbudslovens §§ 67-72 (Lovbekendtgørelse 2025-02-03 nr. 116). Dette indebærer, at alene prækvalificerede har ret til at deltage i dialogfasen og afgive eventuelt tilbud. Enhver økonomisk aktør kan ansøge om deltagelse i udbuddet, og Bygherre vurderer ansøgerens egnethed for den videre deltagelse i udbudsforretningen. Konkurrencepræget dialog giver mulighed for at føre dialog med indbudte dialogdeltagere i dialogfasen med henblik på at kunne indkredse den løsning, der bedst opfylder bygherres behov, hvorefter der overgås til en tilbudsfase, der indeholder den egentlige tilbudsafgivning på baggrund af den/de valgte løsning(er). Nærværende udbud er således inddelt i 3 faser. Først en prækvalifikationsfase, som efterfølges af en dialogfase, som efterfølges af en tilbudsfase. Tilbudsfasen indeholder udsendelse af det endelige udbudsmateriale til alle, der er prækvalificerede til dialogen. Den konkurrenceprægede dialog gennemføres derfor med henblik på at identificere og udvikle de løsninger, der bedst understøtter Projektets målsætninger inden for Projektets rammer. Det Beskrivende Dokument indeholder betingelser for og vejledning om ansøgning om prækvalifikation til deltagelse i dialogfasen og afgivelse af tilbud på ovennævnte udbud. Derudover beskriver dokumentet den opgave, som Arwos udbyder og ønsker løsninger på.

title: Germany – Land rental or sale services – Kartellrechtliches Auswahlverfahren zur Vergabe von Industrie- und Gewerbeflächen im Bereich des Voslapper Groden Nord
description: Der Containerterminal JadeWeserPort wurde offiziell am 21.09.2012 durch den Betreiber, die Eurogate CTW GmbH & Co KG, in Betrieb genommen. Neben dem Containerterminal ist das trimodale Güterverkehrszentrum JadeWeserPort (nachfolgend "GVZ JadeWeserPort") entstanden, welches von dem Eigentümer entwickelt und betrieben wird. Ergänzend hierzu hat JWP-M im Jahr 2026 das Eigentum an Flächen im Bereich des Voslapper Groden Nord (VGN) erworben. Die Flächen des VGN sollen als Energy Hub Cluster mit ggf. trimodaler Anbindung (Wasser-Bahn-Straße) weiterentwickelt und genutzt werden. Für einen Teil der derzeit noch nicht durch Vertragsschluss vergebenen Gewerbeflächen des Industriegebiets mit einer Größe von insgesamt ca. 400.000 m² (im Folgenden: Vermarktungsflächen) sollen mit diesem Auswahlverfahren Grundstücksverträge für Ansiedlungen aus dem Bereich der erneuerbaren Energien und/oder energieintensive Industrien vergeben werden. Hierzu sollen Grundstücksverträge geschlossen werden, die die jeweiligen Ansiedler verpflichten, den Standort möglichst hafenaffin (mit wasserseitigem Umschlag über die bei den Landesgesellschaften des Landes Niedersachsen vorhandenen und in Zukunft zu errichtenden Hafeninfrastrukturen) mit der Zweckbestimmung Industriegebiet für erneuerbare Energien und/oder energieintensive Industrien ("Energy Hub"; im Folgenden: Industriegebiet) dauerhaft zu betreiben. Die Grundstücksverträge werden entsprechende Verpflichtungen zum Bau und zur Inbetriebnahme/zum Betrieb der Betriebsgebäude/Produktionsstätten enthalten.

title: Nedrivning og miljøsanering af Sankt Lukas Vej 7A-7C - Hovedentreprise
description: Gentofte Kommune udbyder som hovedentreprise nedrivning og miljøsanering af den eksisterende bebyggelse på Sankt Lukas Vej 7A-7C, matr.nr. 8li, Gentofte. Nedrivningen klargør grunden til opførelsen af Ny Lindely Plejehjem, som udbydes som totalentreprise i et selvstændigt udbud (TED 607791-2026). Grunden overdrages til totalentreprenøren ved afleveringen. Nedrivningen omfatter ca. 1.980 m² bygningsareal inkl. kælder fordelt på tre adresser, Sankt Lukas Vej 7A, 7B og 7C, samt tilhørende befæstede arealer, fundamenter, terrændæk, installationer og ledningsanlæg. Entreprisen omfatter miljøsanering forud for nedrivningen, herunder fjernelse og bortskaffelse af asbest, PCB, bly og øvrige miljøfarlige stoffer, samt selektiv nedrivning med sortering og genanvendelse af bygge- og anlægsaffald. De gule mursten fra bebyggelsen skal nedtages, afrenses, dokumenteres og opbevares i depot med henblik på genbrug i nybyggeriet. Det tilstødende plejehjem på Sankt Lukas Vej 9A er i fuld drift under hele nedrivningen, og der forventes sideløbende byggeaktivitet på nabomatriklen. Arbejdet skal udføres på en arealmæssigt begrænset byggeplads med delt adgangsvej, begrænsning af støj, støv og vibrationer og koordinering med naboprojektet. Udbuddet omfatter desuden optioner på en midlertidig alternativ vejadgang og nedrivning af en mellemgang mellem Lindely Plejecenter og Sankt Lukas Stiftelsens bygning.

title: Audience Research and Segmentation Studies in Eastern Europe and the Western Balkans
description: International Media Support (IMS) seeks to establish a pool of qualified research providers through framework agreements to deliver recurring audience segmentation studies and related audience intelligence services across Eastern Europe and the Western Balkans. IMS reserves the right to enter into more than one framework agreement as a result of this tender. Across the region, disinformation, information manipulation, and declining trust in information sources continue to affect public discourse and democratic resilience. To design effective responses, media organisations, civil society actors, and other stakeholders require a deeper understanding of audience behaviours, information needs, media consumption habits, levels of trust, and vulnerability to harmful narratives. Through this tender, IMS aims to identify service providers capable of designing and implementing audience segmentation studies and related research in multiple countries across Eastern Europe and the Western Balkans. The findings will support IMS and its partners in developing evidence-based strategies, content, engagement approaches, and interventions that strengthen information integrity and more effectively reach priority audiences. Applications are welcome from research companies, consultancies, academic institutions, and consortia with the required expertise and capacity to deliver high-quality audience research services across the target regions.
